title: Sort by the last digit first?
hook: Three passes, one digit each. Does the order of the passes matter?

knows: stable sorting: ties keep their order
doesNotKnow: that sorting by the least important digit first works
that each later pass decides the order and stability keeps the earlier passes' work

misconception: To sort numbers digit by digit you must start with the first (biggest) digit.
objective: The learner can explain that radix sort deals by the last digit first, then the middle, then the first, and that because each pass keeps ties in order the most important digit has the last word, so three passes sort any list of three-digit numbers.

claims.text: Sorting 329 457 657 839 436 720 355 by the last digit, then the middle digit, then the first digit, keeping ties in their current order, ends fully sorted: 329 355 436 457 657 720 839.
claims.source: Builder's node script (scratchpad verify.mjs): three stable bucket passes in order of place 0, 1, 2 give 720 355 436 457 657 329 839, then 720 329 436 839 355 457 657, then 329 355 436 457 657 720 839, equal to the sorted list. Also agrees with sort on 20,000 random lists of 2-13 three-digit numbers. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 19): Own stable bucket passes (scratchpad fc19b2/radix.mjs): 720 355 436 457 657 329 839 -> 720 329 436 839 355 457 657 -> 329 355 436 457 657 720 839 = sorted.

claims.text: Doing the same passes first digit to last (first digit, then middle, then last) ends 720 355 436 457 657 329 839, which is ordered by the last digit only; the reveal names the first out-of-order pair in the learner's run (720 comes before 355); the first digit went first, so the later passes overwrote its work.
claims.source: Demo.tsx deal() with places 2, 1, 0 from START; builder re-ran in Node (2026-10-14): 329 355 457 436 657 720 839 -> 329 720 436 839 355 457 657 -> 720 355 436 457 657 329 839; last digits 0 5 6 7 7 9 9 ascend. fBad = first i with f[i] > f[i+1] = 0, so the reveal prints '(720 comes before 355)'. v5 corrects the parenthetical per fact-check pass 23 (the v4 claim said 657/329, which the reveal never prints).

claims.text: On pass 3 of last digit first, bucket 3 holds 329 then 355: they tied on the first digit and kept the order the earlier passes had given them, so the earlier digits settle ties and the first digit, dealt last, has the last word. The reveal names this bucket and its cards from the last-digit-first run's own pass-3 buckets; the stage caption reads 'Tie in bucket N: kept the order earlier passes gave it'.
claims.source: Stable pass: bucket contents keep list order (bucket 7 after the first pass holds 457 then 657, as in the input). Radix sort correctness needs each pass stable: CLRS 4th ed. section 8.3 (Lemma 8.3 in the 3rd ed.), whose Figure 8.3 uses this input. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 19): Derivation: Demo.tsx deal() pushes in list order into each bucket and flattens buckets 0-9, so equal-digit cards keep prior order (stable). Inductively after pass p the list is sorted on the last p digits. CLRS 4e 8.3 / Figure 8.3 (this input) from memory, not opened; argument re-derived. | v3 2026-10-14 (demo-builder): the stage now rings the first bucket holding two or more cards on a third pass (bucket 3: 329 then 355 for last-first; bucket 7: 457 then 657 for first-first) with that caption. Reopened. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): Facts verified: last-digit-first pass 3 rings bucket 3 holding 329 then 355, tied on first digit 3, in pass-2 order; stability argument re-derived (CLRS 4e 8.3 from memory, not opened). DISPUTED: the stage shows only the run last touched. Following the explore hint (last first, then first first), the reveal's 'Look at the ringed bucket on pass 3: those cards tied on the first digit' points at the first-digit-first stage, where bucket 7 is ringed holding 457 and 657, which tied on the LAST digit (first digits 4 and 6). The pointer is false on the likely path. Fix (builder): name the bucket in the reveal ('bucket 3 on your last-digit-first pass 3: 329 then 355'), or keep the last-digit-first pass-3 buckets visible. | v4 2026-10-14 (demo-builder): the reveal no longer says 'Look at the ringed bucket'; it reads 'On its pass 3, bucket N held A then B', with N the first bucket of runs.last.buckets holding two or more cards (bucket 3: 329 then 355), so it is true even when the first-digit-first stage is showing. Reopened. | FC pass 23 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Demo.tsx v4 reveal: lb = runs.last.buckets once runs.last.passes === 3. Runs cannot be reset, and the gate needs both runs finished, so lb is always set at the reveal. lt = the first bucket with two or more cards = 3, holding '329 then 355' (own fc23/radix.mjs). The reveal no longer points at the stage, so it holds when the first-digit-first stage (bucket 7 ringed: 457, 657) is on screen. The caption template 'Tie in bucket N: kept the order earlier passes gave it' matches line 147. Stability re-derived from deal(): pushes in list order, flattens 0-9. CLRS 8.3 from memory, not opened; the claim rests on the derivation.

claims.text: Three passes sort three-digit numbers however many there are.
claims.source: CLRS section 8.3: radix sort of n numbers with d digits makes d passes, each a stable sort (time Theta(d(n + k))). Here d = 3. Builder's random check in node over 20,000 lists of 2-13 numbers. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 19): Same induction as c3 with d = 3 places; own random check: 50,000 lists of 1-40 three-digit numbers incl. duplicates, three passes always equal numeric sort.

claims.text: The stage marks each neighbouring pair with < when it is in order and > when it is not.
claims.source: Comparison of adjacent values in the collected list, computed in Demo.tsx; for the pass-2 list 720 329 436 839 355 457 657 the marks are > < < > < <. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 19): Demo.tsx: mark is '<' iff v < next, else '>'; values distinct so no equal case. Own run of pass-2 list gives > < < > < <.

recall.question: Radix sort deals 3-digit numbers into buckets one digit at a time, keeping ties in order. Which digit should the LAST pass use?
options: Any digit; the order does not matter
recall.why: The last pass has the last word. Earlier passes survive only as the order of ties, so the most important digit goes last.
